head: working-tree
subject: MQTT retained benchmark uses harnessz sampling and baseline gating
change: bench_mqtt_retained previously used hand-written timing loops with fixed iteration counts and no baseline support. It now uses examples/support/bench_sampling.zig for warmup plus repeated samples and reports min/p50/p90/p99/mean/stddev per scenario. Five named scenarios cover exact lookup, the broad devices/+/state scan, the devices/# prefix hash, the selective devices/+/state scan on the 16,384-message mixed store, and the selective devices/1234/# subtree. The benchmark accepts --scenario, --samples, --warmup, --baseline, --update-baseline, --warn-only and --max-regression-ratio, and is registered in the bench-record and bench-gate sets with benchmarks/baselines/mqtt-retained.json. The exact scenario now uses a constant filter, so it measures the lookup instead of also formatting a topic string per iteration.

benchmark.command: zig build bench-record -Doptimize=ReleaseFast (records all sampler-backed baselines)

baseline_record.note: recorded seven baseline files, 27 scenario entries in total, including the five retained scenarios

gate.note: the gate compared all seven benchmarks against the recorded baselines and reported 10-21% apparent slowdowns on unchanged binaries while other host sessions were active; this matches the documented host-load limitation and needs a quiet-host confirmation

notes: The sampler medians match the previous fixed-loop benchmark within host noise: devices/+/state 69.5 us/op, devices/# 30.1 us/op, selective devices/+/state 105.7 us/op, devices/1234/# 273 ns/op. Exact lookup reports about 20 ns/op because the old loop formatted devices/<n>/state with std.fmt.bufPrint on every iteration; the new loop reuses one constant filter. The baseline files under benchmarks/baselines/ are local generated artifacts, not tracked sources. Pinning with taskset changes the environment fingerprint because the fingerprint includes the process CPU count, so a pinned gate must be compared against a pinned record. The bench-record and bench-gate steps now depend on each other in build.zig, so the benchmarks run one at a time even when the build runner is parallel; a quiet host is still required for a gate verdict.
